recorded: Every case passed against the original with Node.js 26.12.1, tsx 4.23.1, @huggingface/transformers 4.2.0 with onnxruntime-node 1.24.3, @langchain/core 0.3.80, @langchain/langgraph 0.2.74, @langchain/openai 0.3.17, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0, express 4.22.2, and zod 3.25.76, run as "node --import tsx src/{program}.ts". Unit 8's API matches the source of units 6 and 7 file for file, so this file reuses unit 6's cases, which replay the exchanges recorded from unit 6's copy. The original always calls OpenRouter's address and the public status pages of GitHub and Cloudflare, so the copy these cases run against reads OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPSPILOT_GITHUB_STATUS_URL, and OPSPILOT_CLOUDFLARE_STATUS_URL first and falls back to those addresses, a one-line change in the model factory and two in the status tool, and the cases point the status pages to the replay. No OpenRouter key was available, so the model answers were recorded from Ollama 0.40.11 through its OpenAI-compatible API, with gemma4:12b-mlx standing in for openai/gpt-4o-mini and for the fallback model and without the stand-in's reasoning field, while the requests keep the model the program asked for. The failures of the primary and the fallback models are synthesized from OpenRouter's documented errors (503 when no provider is available, 429 for a rate limit, and 401 for a missing key), and so is the router answer whose route is outside the schema. The cases where models fail send a request to organize the shift, because the turn then waits for the reflector, so every retried call happens in a fixed order, and the one to two seconds each retry waits are never timed. The nine-turn conversation that summarizes its history was recorded with the stand-in's reasoning turned off, which keeps every turn well within the chat API's 180-second timeout, and none of its messages teaches a fact, so none of its recalls depends on a score. The status pages were recorded from the real ones on 2026-10-27, and the failing page is synthesized. Embeddings come from Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, which the first run downloads from the Hugging Face hub, and sentence-transformers' all-MiniLM-L6-v2 in Python gives the same scores to four decimals. Every score that decides a recall, its order, or a duplicate stays at least 0.02 from its threshold and from its neighbors. The chat server and the MCP server keep their SQLite database at data/opspilot.db, which each of their cases starts without and checks afterwards. The chat server asks the reflector about every turn without waiting for it, so its cases wait a second after every response. The replay serves each recorded answer to the call whose model and system prompt match, while the cases check the calls in the original's order. Token estimates, promptTokens, and the stats' tokens and costs follow from the replayed texts and usage, so they are compared exactly. Request, approval, incident, conversation, and memory ids, times, and latencies vary, so they are checked by shape and by reuse, and the log lines are compared exactly apart from them, the lines of one request sharing its id. Tool results that carry an incident id are checked by their call id only, and no case resolves an incident it has just opened. An MCP server may report invalid arguments and unknown tools as a tool result with isError or as a JSON-RPC error with code -32602, and validation errors are checked by their error code and a non-empty list of issues, because every validator words them differently. The arena's message about a missing key is checked by its first sentence, because the rest suggests Node.js commands.
